entities.headline: Tangela in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Its real body is hidden beneath a mass of constantly growing blue vines, making its true appearance one of Pokémon’s long-running little mysteries.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Tangrowth in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Its arms are bundles of vines that can stretch and regrow, so losing a vine is hardly a problem for this powerful Grass-type.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Pinsir in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: It is famous for enormous pincers and remarkable strength, using those horns to grab, lift, and crush opponents.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Spinarak in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: The web pattern on its back resembles a face, and its strong silk can be used to make sturdy fishing nets.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Ariados in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: A nocturnal spider Pokémon that uses silk from both its mouth and abdomen to trap prey and mark trails.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Sunkern in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: One of the smallest and lightest Pokémon, it stores nutrients while waiting for the chance to evolve into Sunflora.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Sunflora in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: It converts sunlight into energy and becomes much more active in bright daylight, fitting its sunflower-like design perfectly.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Heracross in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: This rhinoceros-beetle Pokémon is astonishingly strong and is known for lifting objects many times its own weight.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Volbeat in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Its glowing tail is used to communicate and to draw patterns in the night sky, often in connection with Illumise.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Illumise in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: It guides groups of Volbeat to create glowing patterns in the night sky, giving the pair one of Pokémon’s most unusual partnerships.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Leafeon in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: An Eevee evolution adapted to forests; its cells behave somewhat like plants and can produce energy from sunlight.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Phantump in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Folklore says this little Ghost-type is a spirit inhabiting a tree stump, giving its cute appearance a slightly eerie edge.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Trevenant in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: It can control trees with its roots and is fiercely protective of forests, especially against people who harm woodland Pokémon.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Grookey in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: It carries a special stick from its forest home and creates rhythm by tapping it against objects.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Thwackey in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Its sense of rhythm becomes more important as it evolves, and it practices drumming almost obsessively.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Rillaboom in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: A powerful drummer whose beats can control roots and plants; its design turns Grookey’s tiny stick into a full drum kit.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Applin in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: A tiny dragon that hides inside an apple, borrowing the fruit as both shelter and disguise.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Dipplin in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: This Kitakami evolution of Applin lives inside a syrup-coated apple and is actually formed by two creatures working together.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Iron Leaves in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: A futuristic Paradox Pokémon resembling Virizion, with glowing blade-like horns and a sleek mechanical appearance.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: A Haunted Cup of Matcha
entities.lore_fact: It resembles Sinistea but is unrelated; it is a matcha-based Ghost Pokémon said to have formed from the regrets of a tea master.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Tea with a Ghostly Twist
entities.lore_fact: The evolution of Poltchageist lives in a fine teacup and builds energy by stirring with the tea whisk on its head.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: The Face of Kitakami
entities.lore_fact: Ogerpon is the central Legendary Pokémon of Kitakami’s Teal Mask story, and this mask represents its natural Grass-type form.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Vulpix in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: It is born with a single pale tail that gradually divides into six beautiful curled tails as it grows.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Ninetales in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Its nine tails are tied to old legends, and stories warn that mistreating one can bring a very long-lasting curse.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Slugma in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Its body is made of extremely hot magma; if it stops moving, its molten body can begin to harden.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Magcargo in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Its shell is hardened magma, while the inside remains incredibly hot—one of the most volcanically themed Pokémon in the series.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Torkoal in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: It burns coal inside its shell and releases smoke from its nostrils and back, with the smoke revealing how healthy it is.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Chimchar in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Its tail flame is produced by burning gas in its belly and can even go out when it sleeps.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Monferno in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: It intimidates enemies with the flame on its tail and uses walls and ceilings to attack from unexpected angles.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Infernape in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Inspired by the Monkey King, it combines acrobatics, martial arts, and blazing punches in a fast, aggressive fighting style.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Darumaka in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: It stores heat inside its body and becomes extremely energetic when that internal fire is burning strongly.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Darmanitan in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Known for explosive physical power, it can switch between very different battle styles depending on form and ability.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Litwick in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Its candle flame looks welcoming, but Pokédex lore says it can absorb life energy from those who follow its light.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Lampent in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: It is often associated with hospitals and places where life is fading, making it one of the darker Ghost-type designs.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Chandelure in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Its eerie flames are said to burn spirits rather than bodies, fitting its haunted chandelier design.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Chi-Yu in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: One of Paldea’s Treasures of Ruin, it was born from beads linked to human envy and can melt rock with intense flames.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Ogerpon’s Fiery Mask
entities.lore_fact: With the Hearthflame Mask, Ogerpon takes on a fiery Grass/Fire form associated with a fierce, aggressive fighting style.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Poliwag in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Its transparent belly shows a spiral-shaped internal organ pattern, one of the oldest visual quirks in the Pokédex.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Poliwhirl in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: The spiral on its belly can mesmerize opponents, and its newly developed arms make it much more capable on land.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Poliwrath in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: A superb swimmer with powerful muscles; it can cross large bodies of water using multiple swimming styles.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Goldeen in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Its elegant fins make it look like a dancer underwater, but its horn can be surprisingly dangerous.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Seaking in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: During breeding season it swims upstream and uses its horn to carve nests into rocks.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Jynx in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Its dance-like movements and unusual vocalizations have always made it one of the series’ most distinctive humanoid Pokémon.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Corphish in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Originally from overseas, it is extremely hardy and can thrive even in polluted or stagnant water.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Crawdaunt in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Aggressive and territorial, it uses its massive claws to drive nearly everything else away from its pond.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Feebas in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Famously shabby-looking and extremely hardy, it can survive in poor water conditions before evolving into the elegant Milotic.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Milotic in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Often described as one of the most beautiful Pokémon, it is said to calm anger and conflict with its soothing presence.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Snorunt in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: It survives in snowy regions and is said in folklore to bring prosperity to homes it visits.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Glalie in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: It freezes moisture in the air into armor and can rapidly freeze prey with icy breath.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Froslass in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Inspired by the Japanese yuki-onna snow spirit, it is associated with icy mountains and eerie frozen victims.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Glaceon in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: An Eevee evolution that lowers its body temperature to freeze moisture in the air into glittering ice crystals.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Phione in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: A small sea-dwelling Mythical Pokémon that drifts in warm oceans and can always return to its birthplace.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Froakie in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: It protects itself with flexible bubbles called Frubbles, which cushion blows and hide how light and agile it is.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Frogadier in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: It can throw bubble-covered pebbles with surprising accuracy and move rapidly through trees and rocky terrain.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Cramorant in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Its Gulp Missile gimmick has it dive for prey and sometimes return with something far more surprising than a fish.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Finizen in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: A playful dolphin Pokémon that uses the water ring around its tail and bonds closely with companions.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: A Secret Superhero
entities.lore_fact: Its ordinary Zero Form hides a superhero transformation: after switching out in battle, it returns as the dramatically stronger Hero Form.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Iron Bundle in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: A futuristic Paradox Pokémon resembling Delibird, with a robotic body and a water cannon hidden in its tail-like sack.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Walking Wake in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: An ancient-looking Paradox Pokémon resembling Suicune, reimagined as a powerful reptilian creature.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Ogerpon of the Wellspring
entities.lore_fact: The Wellspring Mask changes Ogerpon into a Grass/Water form, connecting it with flowing water and a more graceful battle style.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Zapdos in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: One of Kanto’s legendary birds, associated with thunderstorms and crackling electricity.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Shinx in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Its muscles generate electricity when they move, causing its fur to glow before it releases a shock.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Luxio in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Its claws can channel electricity, allowing members of a group to communicate or stun opponents.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Luxray in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Its extraordinary eyesight can see through solid objects, helping it locate hidden prey or missing young.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Emolga in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: A flying squirrel Pokémon that stores electricity in its cheeks and glides using membrane-like flaps between its limbs.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Helioptile in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: It spreads the frills on its head to absorb sunlight and generate enough electricity to power itself without eating.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Heliolisk in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Its solar-powered frills can generate impressive amounts of electricity, matching its desert-lizard inspiration.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Morpeko in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Its Hunger Switch changes both its mood and appearance, flipping between Full Belly and Hangry modes.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Tadbulb in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: It floats using electricity generated by shaking its tail and can light up its whole body like a tiny bulb.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Bellibolt in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Its eye-like bumps are actually false eyes; the real eyes are the small yellow dots above its mouth.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Wattrel in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: A seabird Pokémon that uses wind and its wings to generate electricity while flying over the ocean.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Kilowattrel in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: It combines the speed of a seabird with powerful electrical organs, storing energy in its throat sac.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Iron Thorns in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: A futuristic Paradox Pokémon resembling Tyranitar, covered in angular armor and glowing green elements.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Clefairy in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Long associated with the moon, it is famously shy and said to gather under moonlight on special nights.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Clefable in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Its sensitive hearing lets it detect tiny sounds from far away, and it prefers quiet mountain areas.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Abra in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: It sleeps for most of the day but can teleport even while asleep when it senses danger.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Kadabra in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Its psychic powers are so strong that electronics can malfunction nearby, and it amplifies them with its spoon.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Alakazam in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Its brain continues growing throughout its life, giving it extraordinary memory and psychic intelligence.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Girafarig in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Its tail has a small brain of its own and can react independently, even biting enemies behind it.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Farigiraf in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: After evolving, Girafarig’s tail-head merges over its main head like a protective helmet, boosting its psychic power.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Chimecho in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: It creates sound by vibrating its body and uses its long tail to hang from branches or structures.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Flabébé in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: It bonds with a single flower soon after birth and carries that flower for the rest of its life.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Floette in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: It draws power from flowers and is particularly associated with beautifully maintained gardens.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Florges in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: It controls flower gardens and can live for centuries, turning floral energy into powerful Fairy-type attacks.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Swirlix in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Its body is as light and sweet as cotton candy because it eats almost nothing but sugary foods.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Slurpuff in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Its incredible sense of smell is millions of times more sensitive than a human’s, making it excellent at identifying scents.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Sandygast in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: A possessed pile of sand that can compel people and Pokémon to add more sand to its body.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Palossand in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: It controls sand to trap prey and grows into a haunted sandcastle large enough to dominate a beach.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Enamorus in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: A Legendary Pokémon associated with spring; its arrival is said to signal the end of harsh winter weather.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Scream Tail in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: An ancient Paradox Pokémon resembling Jigglypuff but with fangs, wild hair, and a much more feral appearance.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Brains of the Loyal Three
entities.lore_fact: One of Kitakami’s so-called Loyal Three; its chain is linked to heightened cleverness and strong psychic abilities.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Beauty of the Loyal Three
entities.lore_fact: One of the Loyal Three, known for beauty and charm enhanced by the strange chain around its body.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Sandshrew in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Its dry, tough hide lets it thrive in deserts, and it curls into a ball to protect itself from danger.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Sandslash in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Its back is covered in hard spikes, and it can curl into a defensive ball or slash with long claws.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Hisuian Growlithe in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: This regional Growlithe has thick fur and a rocky horn, adaptations suited to the colder Hisui region.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Hisuian Arcanine in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Its Hisuian form combines Fire and Rock traits and has a much more rugged, volcanic look than the familiar Arcanine.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Nosepass in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Its magnetic nose always points north, making groups of Nosepass unable to face one another directly.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Probopass in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: It controls three small magnetic units called Mini-Noses and uses magnetism to attack and navigate.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Timburr in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: It always carries a wooden beam and uses it both for training and for construction work.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Gurdurr in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: It carries an iron beam to strengthen itself and is skilled enough to help build large structures.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Conkeldurr in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: It is said to have taught humans how to make concrete, fighting with two massive concrete pillars.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Greninja in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: A ninja-inspired Pokémon that creates sharp water weapons and moves with exceptional speed and stealth.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Hawlucha in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: A luchador-inspired Pokémon that fights with dramatic aerial wrestling moves and uses its wings for balance.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Glimmet in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Its mineral-like petals contain poison, and it clings to cave walls where it absorbs nutrients from stone.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Glimmora in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Its toxic crystal petals open like a flower when threatened, scattering poisonous material around it.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Ting-Lu in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: One of the Treasures of Ruin, formed around a ritual vessel and powerful enough to split the earth with its weight.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: One of the Loyal Three
entities.lore_fact: One of Kitakami’s Loyal Three; the chain around its neck greatly increased its physical strength.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Ogerpon Stands Like Stone
entities.lore_fact: The Cornerstone Mask gives Ogerpon a Grass/Rock form built around toughness, defense, and a stone-like stance.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Poochyena in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: It has an excellent sense of smell and will chase prey persistently, though it can lose nerve against stronger foes.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Mightyena in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: It lives and hunts in packs with strict social order, following experienced leaders with impressive discipline.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Venipede in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: It senses its surroundings with the feelers on its head and tail and injects poison through sharp fangs.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Whirlipede in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: It is protected by a hard shell and can roll at high speed, building momentum before striking.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Scolipede in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: A huge centipede Pokémon that chases prey relentlessly and attacks with toxic horns on its head.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Brute Bonnet in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: An ancient Paradox Pokémon resembling Amoonguss, but with a rougher, more prehistoric body.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Skarmory in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Its metal feathers are razor-sharp, and despite its armored body it can fly at surprisingly high speed.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Aron in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: It eats iron ore—and sometimes man-made metal—to build the tough armor covering its body.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Lairon in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: It lives in mountains rich in iron and fiercely defends feeding territory from rivals.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Aggron in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: A heavily armored Pokémon that treats an entire mountain as its territory and repairs environmental damage there.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Heatran in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: A Legendary Pokémon with a body of molten steel, found crawling across volcanic cave walls using cross-shaped claws.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Varoom in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: A Poison/Steel Pokémon formed when a mysterious substance entered an abandoned engine and brought it to life.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Revavroom in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: An engine-like Pokémon that uses toxic exhaust and multiple cylinders to generate tremendous power.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Dreepy in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: A tiny Dragon/Ghost Pokémon based on an ancient species; it is weak alone and often stays near stronger evolutions.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Drakloak in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: It carries Dreepy on its head and will search for another one if separated, making the evolution line unusually family-like.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Dragapult in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: It launches the Dreepy living in its horn-like head openings at high speed—apparently with the Dreepy enjoying the ride.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Tiny Sushi, Big Brain
entities.lore_fact: A tiny sushi-like Dragon Pokémon that is extremely intelligent and forms a famous partnership with Dondozo.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Farfetch'd in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: It carries a leek-like stalk as a weapon and tool; the stalk is so important that it carefully chooses and protects it.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Chansey in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Known for kindness and healing, it carries a nutritious egg and often shares it with injured people or Pokémon.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Blissey in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: The evolved form of Chansey is strongly associated with compassion and healing, and its egg is said to make people feel happier.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: The Evolution Pokémon
entities.lore_fact: Its unstable genetic structure lets it evolve into many different forms, making it the symbol of branching evolution in Pokémon.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Snorlax in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: It spends most of its time eating and sleeping, but can digest almost anything and is incredibly powerful when motivated.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Aipom in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Its hand-like tail is so useful for climbing and grabbing that its actual arms have become comparatively less important.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Ambipom in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: After evolving, it gains two hand-like tails and uses them with remarkable dexterity for almost everything.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Ducklett in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: It is an excellent swimmer and sprays water from its feathers while preening to keep them clean.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Swanna in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: It dances elegantly at dusk and can fly for thousands of miles using powerful wings.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: The Bloodmoon Beast
entities.lore_fact: The mysterious “Bloodmoon Beast” is a unique Ursaluna found in Kitakami, marked by a red moon-like feature on its forehead and the signature move Blood Moon.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Accompanying Flute in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: A Kitakami-flavored Item card whose flute imagery fits the set’s festival and folklore atmosphere.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Bug Catching Set in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: A Trainer Item themed around catching and studying bugs, matching the rural, outdoorsy feel of Kitakami.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Caretaker in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: A Supporter representing one of the adults connected with Blueberry Academy and the wider Scarlet & Violet school setting.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Kitakami’s Fierce Big Sister
entities.lore_fact: A major character from The Teal Mask. She is Kieran’s older sister: proud, competitive, and deeply connected to Kitakami.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Community Center in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: A Stadium tied directly to Kitakami’s village life and the communal setting seen throughout The Teal Mask story.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Cook in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: A Supporter built around the simple Pokémon-world idea of preparing food to help your team.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Enhanced Hammer in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: A returning disruptive Item with a long TCG history; its identity is all about removing troublesome Special Energy.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: A Festival of Mischief & Mystery
entities.lore_fact: A Stadium that captures Twilight Masquerade’s central Kitakami festival theme more directly than almost any other card in the set.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Handheld Fan in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: A Pokémon Tool with a festival accessory look, fitting the warm-weather celebration aesthetic of Kitakami.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Hassel in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: An Elite Four member and art teacher from Paldea, known for his dramatic personality and deep love of art.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Hyper Aroma in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: An ACE SPEC Item—meaning you can include only one ACE SPEC card in your deck—centered on finding Evolution Pokémon.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Jamming Tower in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: A Stadium themed around interference, mechanically fitting the idea of shutting down or disrupting equipment.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: The Boy Who Idolized Ogerpon
entities.lore_fact: A central character in The Teal Mask whose admiration for Ogerpon becomes a major part of his personal story and rivalry with the player.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Lana's Aid in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: A Supporter featuring Lana, the Water-type Trial Captain from Alola, returning here as a useful recovery-themed Trainer card.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Love Ball in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: A Poké Ball originally introduced in Johto, designed around the idea of catching Pokémon of the same species and opposite gender.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Lucian in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: A Psychic-type Elite Four member from Sinnoh, recognizable for his calm, scholarly personality and love of reading.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Lucky Helmet in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: A Pokémon Tool whose protective helmet theme is paired with a reward when the attached Pokémon is attacked.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Ogre's Mask in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: An Item directly tied to Ogerpon’s masks, the central objects behind Twilight Masquerade’s Kitakami story and its four Ogerpon forms.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Hunting the Bloodmoon Beast
entities.lore_fact: A photographer introduced in The Teal Mask who asks the player to help photograph rare Pokémon and is closely linked to the Bloodmoon Ursaluna quest.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Raifort in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: Paldea’s history teacher, fascinated by legends and ancient mysteries—including the Treasures of Ruin.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Scoop Up Cyclone in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: A returning ACE SPEC Item with a classic TCG identity: a powerful one-per-deck way to pick up one of your Pokémon and its attached cards.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Secret Box in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: An ACE SPEC Item themed around trading resources for access to several different Trainer-card options.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Survival Brace in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: An ACE SPEC Pokémon Tool designed around surviving a hit that would otherwise Knock Out the attached Pokémon.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Unfair Stamp in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: An ACE SPEC Item that becomes especially disruptive after one of your Pokémon has been Knocked Out.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Boomerang Energy in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: A Special Energy whose identity is exactly what the name suggests: it can return after being discarded under the right condition.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Legacy Energy in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: An ACE SPEC Special Energy and one of the set’s most unusual cards, because ACE SPEC rules normally make these cards one-per-deck choices.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Buddy-Buddy Poffin in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: A popular Item for setting up small Basic Pokémon early, themed after the Poffins used as Pokémon treats in Sinnoh.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Rescue Board in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: A Pokémon Tool built around making a Pokémon easier to retreat, especially when it has taken damage.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text

entities.headline: Luminous Energy in the Spotlight
entities.lore_fact: A flexible Special Energy that can provide different Energy types, but with restrictions that reward careful deck building.
entities.source_basis: Pokemon.com Pokédex / official game lore / card flavor text
